executive_summary: Five recent, actionable security advisories covering privilege escalation, file write flaws, authentication bypass, container security, and DoS via SVG parsing. All are suitable for hands‑on lab exercises and portfolio projects.

signals.title: Zammad improper privilege management (CVE-2026-102490)
signals.what_changed: Local zammad user can escalate privileges to root due to improper privilege management.
signals.why_it_matters: Privilege escalation gives full system control, a common post‑exploitation goal.
signals.application: Deploy a Zammad instance in a VM, reproduce the escalation, and practice detection with audit logs and SELinux/AppArmor policies.

signals.title: Fortinet FortiMail path traversal & NULL byte (CVE-2026-104286)
signals.what_changed: Unauthenticated attacker can write arbitrary files via crafted HTTP/HTTPS requests using path traversal and NULL‑byte tricks.
signals.why_it_matters: Arbitrary file write can lead to remote code execution and system compromise.
signals.application: Spin up a FortiMail sandbox, craft malicious requests, and verify mitigations such as input validation and path canonicalization.

signals.title: Cisco Catalyst SD‑WAN Manager hex‑encoding handling (CVE-2026-76504)
signals.what_changed: Improper URI hex‑encoding handling lets an unauthenticated remote attacker obtain admin‑level access.
signals.why_it_matters: Admin access enables configuration changes and data exfiltration.
signals.application: Use a SD‑WAN manager VM, test URI encoding bypasses, and implement strict request parsing and authentication checks.

signals.title: gitea‑runner passes host namespaces/capabilities when privileged mode disabled (GHSA‑x4q3‑gcj3‑m6cf)
signals.what_changed: Workflow container.options propagates host namespaces and capability flags even though privileged mode is off.
signals.why_it_matters: Potential container breakout and host compromise.
signals.application: Create a Gitea runner container, inspect the options, and enforce secure defaults (drop unnecessary namespaces/capabilities).

signals.title: probe‑image‑size quadratic‑time DoS in SVG parser (GHSA‑gjj5‑9665‑rwrc)
signals.what_changed: SVG parser processes specially crafted SVGs with quadratic time complexity, causing CPU exhaustion.
signals.why_it_matters: Denial‑of‑service via resource exhaustion impacts availability.
signals.application: Build a small Node.js service using probe‑image‑size, feed malicious SVGs, and implement rate limiting and input sanitization.

experiment.title: Lab: Privilege Escalation & File Write Chains in Zammad & FortiMail
experiment.objective: Reproduce two CISA‑tracked vulnerabilities (Zammad LPE and FortiMail path traversal) in isolated VMs to practice detection, exploitation, and mitigation.
steps: 1. Spin up two VMs: Zammad (latest stable) and FortiMail (trial image).
2. Update both to the latest patches to confirm vendor fixes.

3. For Zammad: enable debug logging, create a low‑privilege zammad user, and run a script that attempts to abuse the improper privilege management (e.g., set‑uid binary). Capture logs showing root access.
4. For FortiMail: craft a malicious HTTP request with path traversal and NULL‑byte to write a test file to /var/www/html/. Use curl with encoded payloads.
5. Verify file creation and execute the file to confirm RCE potential.
6. Document findings, create a remediation plan (input validation, principle of least privilege, patched versions).
7. Clean up VMs and export evidence (screenshots, logs, request/response) for portfolio.
expected_evidence: Zammad logs showing root‑level process execution from zammad user.
FortiMail filesystem listing confirming arbitrary file write.
experiment.stop_condition: All steps completed or 60 minutes elapsed, whichever comes first.
